posts.body:
Those are also two unrelated event pages that I can tell. The first you only showed the screenshot of page 1, not page 2. The 2nd is page 1 of a different event.
Note that self switches have no bearing on new events. They only work on that one event. That's why it has the word self in it. So not sure why you have a self switch A ON in that first event either, as it really does nothing that needs to be done.

Look, here is page one of a character on the map:
Here is page 2 of that same character.
If the actor is in the party, the event is hidden, if the actor is not in the party, the event shows.
If you want it the other way around, that the event only shows up when the actor is in the party, simply do this:
Because the condition is now on the page with the character, it won't show if the condition isn't met. In this case a second page is not needed.

No problem!
I do have 2 pieces of advice to you:
1.
I tell this to all beginners. I see you have RPG maker for 2 years, or at least have your account for 2 years, but this is a beginner mistake, so I will give you the same advice: Explore all the basics of RPG maker. See a button, and you don't know what it does? Press it and see what happens.
Do this for all the buttons, and the buttons in the windows that show up after you press the buttons. When you don't know what something does, hover over it. A little help window will show up.
The very most important things that users should learn first are:
Switches
Variables
Conditions/Conditional branches
You should learn what Conditions are and how they are used, and what conditional branches are and how they are used. Because they are 2 completely different functions in the engine.
2.
I did see your problem, but a few other responders that have even more experience than I do did not see it, because the information just wasn't there. I honestly guessed it.
Okay, it wasn't completely a guess... I have have plenty experience teaching new users. I saw what you did, imagined what you tried to do, and filled in the blancs in between.
Not everyone here is used to teach people who have a lesser understanding of the engine then they do. That is why most users will assume you are at least familiar with the basics. This is probably why other responders didn't recognize your problem: They saw what you did, but didn't recognize what you tried to achieve.
So, like others have said before, make sure your information is complete. The more complete your request for help is, the faster and better the answer will be.
(This is no reason for getting an attitude from people who claim to help, though. I think some people forgot that this is supposed to be an entertaining activity for the most of us. I really envy your ability to just scroll past those, while still paying attention to the helpful replies that come after.)
